verification.reasoning: $89 spread over 18 months of expected life is $4.944 a month, which rounds to $4.94.
$164 over 36 months is $4.5555 a month, which rounds to $4.56.
$52 over 8 months is exactly $6.50 a month, the highest of the three despite the lowest sticker price.
The Kestrel Pro is excluded before any price comparison because it is wireless only; between the two wired models, $4.94 a month beats $6.50.

Headphones are bought whole. Two Arias last 36 months exactly, at $178. Four Dunlins reach only month 32, so covering 36 months takes five, at $260. The difference is $82.00 — larger than the per-month rates suggest, because the fifth Dunlin is bought in full for four months of use.

judgment.prompt: The Kestrel Pro has the lowest cost per month of the three. Explain why it is still the wrong purchase here.
acceptableAnswerCriteria: States that the Kestrel Pro cannot do the job at all, because the simulated equipment has no wireless option, so its $4.56 a month buys nothing usable.
Distinguishes fitness for purpose as a requirement to be met before price is compared, not as one factor traded off against price.
evidenceRequirements: Cites the wired-jack requirement from the scenario and the Kestrel Pro’s $4.56 figure together.
lookFors: The response screens on the requirement first and prices second, rather than arguing the Kestrel is "worth a bit more".
The response does not treat the wired requirement as a preference.
judgment.commonMisconception: Treating every attribute as a tradeoff, including one that decides whether the product works at all.

judgment.prompt: The Dunlin has the lowest sticker price and the highest cost per month. Explain how both can be true.
acceptableAnswerCriteria: Explains that cost per month divides price by expected life, so a cheap item that lasts 8 months can cost more per month than a dearer one lasting 18.
Uses the two figures, $52 over 8 months against $89 over 18 months, rather than asserting the general point.
evidenceRequirements: Quotes both the sticker prices and both the expected lifespans.
lookFors: The response identifies expected life as the second variable, not "quality" in general.

oracle.method: every fixed answer above was recomputed from the item's own stated scenario parameters, not transcribed
oracle.arithmetic: exact rational arithmetic over BigInt; no binary floating point
oracle.limits: Recomputation establishes that the key follows from the stated figures. It does not by itself establish that the model chosen is the right model for the scenario; that is carried by the per-item reasoning, the parameter-visibility check, and human review.
